description.value: Aburi To-Go bills itself as Vancouver's first 'grocerant' — a hybrid grocery store and restaurant — offering fresh Japanese ready-to-eat meals, daily bento boxes, onigiri, ramen kits, house-made sauces, and imported Japanese snacks in the Yaletown neighbourhood. Founded in 2020 as an extension of the acclaimed Aburi Restaurants Canada group (behind Miku and Minami), it sits directly next to Minami Restaurant on Mainland Street. Cyclists riding the nearby seawall or passing through Yaletown will find a wide selection of travel-friendly packaged meals and plant-based options well-suited to the road.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Aburi To-Go is an operational Japanese grocerant offering grab-and-go packaged meals, bento, onigiri, and plant-based SHOJIN items — supporting Takeout, Packed lunches, and Vegetarian/vegan amenities. The contact page shows a different phone number, (604) 428-6799, than OSM's +1-604-685-8080, so the website value is used and the discrepancy flagged. No cycling-specific amenities (bike parking, water refill, washrooms, Wi-Fi, charging) are mentioned anywhere on the site.
concerns: Phone number mismatch: OSM lists +1-604-685-8080 but the website contact page shows (604) 428-6799; the website value has been used.
Email mismatch: OSM lists aburitogo@aburirestaurants.com but the website contact page shows groceryclerk@aburirestaurants.com.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Legitimate, active food stop in a high-cycling-traffic corridor adjacent to the Yaletown seawall; grab-and-go bento, onigiri, and packaged meals are well-suited to touring cyclists seeking a quick, quality Japanese meal in downtown Vancouver.

Packed lunches.detail: Daily bento boxes, Ready-to-Eat packaged salads, sando sandwiches, and bowls available as grab-and-go items

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: SHOJIN plant-based line: 'daily chef-crafted in-house items, as well as exclusive imports from Japan. Available at both Aburi To-Go locations.'
